title: Geometric and coefficient-domain realization of base change
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are separated of finite type. At $A_n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,A_n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category; at $R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$. Integral categories use completed coefficient sheaves and derived completeness with reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; field categories use rationalization and common finite coefficient-field stages, respectively. 

Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\prime\to Y$, $g\prime:X\prime\to X$ and $f\prime:X\prime\to Y\prime$ form a Cartesian square, so $f g\prime=g f\prime$ and $X\prime\simeq X\times_Y Y\prime$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Use the adjunction-mate ordinary exchange and the compactification-defined compact-support exchange [def-exchange-projection], with completed integral pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Every corner is Noetherian, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and of finite dimension. There is a nonnegative uniform bound on the dimensions of all geometric fibres of $f$, including empty fibres; if $f$ is proper, so is $f'$. Compactifications exist, and their open factors are quasi-compact.
The actual exchanges
$$g^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^*K,\qquad g^*Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!g'^*K$$
have the following isomorphism domains. For the first map require $f$ proper or $g$ smooth. At finite etale coefficients use bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology; its pro-etale transport requires an etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], bounded constructible in the smooth case. At integral coefficients use the completed exchange and compatible finite-reduction etale-origin witnesses. At $E$ use a specified admissible integral lattice and the raw rationalized exchange; at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use admissible common-stage representatives stable under finite overfields. For smooth exchange the lattice and comparison hypotheses are exactly those of [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] and [sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch]; a conclusion in $D^b_c$ additionally requires the uniform finite-level constructibility and interval bounds stated there. Without those landing bounds only the ambient completed isomorphism is asserted.
For the second map no smoothness of $g$ is needed. Use bounded finite torsion etale inputs, their witnessed finite pro-etale transports, and at integral and field stages the derived-complete constructible inputs with compatible etale-origin reductions and the specified lattice/common-stage presentations and uniform landing bounds of [thm-cbc-complete-proetale], [thm-cbc-finite-extension], [thm-cbc-qbar]. The maps coincide with those supplied by the respective finite, completed and transported base-change theorems, and respect identity, pasting, refinement and composition on those domains. No exchange for discrete non-torsion coefficients on the small etale site is asserted.

proof.text: For each corner $T$, the structure map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite type. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] it is quasi-separated, and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives finite dimension. Apply (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to each arrow: its source is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and its target is quasi-separated, so the arrow is qcqs. Finally $\ell$ is invertible on every corner: the nonzero element $\ell\in k$ has an inverse and the structure ring maps preserve this inverse. Thus the qcqs, Noetherian, finite-dimensional and invertible-prime hypotheses required below hold at the actual input and output corners, including $Y'$ as the output of exchange.

Since $Y$ is quasi-compact and $f$ finite type, [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] supplies $e\geq0$ with $\dim X_y\leq e$ for all $y$. Each $X_y$ is finite type over $\kappa(y)$; the field-extension assertion of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] gives $\dim X_{\bar y}=\dim X_y\leq e$. Empty fibres have dimension $-\infty$, so the same nonnegative $e$ includes them. If $f$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] makes $f'$ proper. Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to $f$ over the qcqs target $Y$ to obtain a compactification. By [def-nagata-compactification] its open factor is quasi-compact. These verifications also apply to any other separated finite-type map to a corner for which a compactification is needed in a composition diagram.

source.place: Clause (4): fibre bound and compactifications; Stacks 0A3V (lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension).

proof.text: Verify the coefficient input rather than identifying different ambient categories. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $R$ is a domain DVR with finite residue field and maximal ideal $(\varpi)$. Its absolute value is nonarchimedean, as the next lemma requires: if $|x|\le|y|$ with $y\ne0$, then $x/y\in R$, so $1+x/y\in R$ because $R$ is a subring, and $|x+y|=|y|\,|1+x/y|\le|y|$. It is Noetherian since every ideal in a PID is generated by one element. The restriction of the absolute value to $\mathbf Q_\ell$ gives $|\ell|<1$, so the residue field has characteristic $\ell$. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $A_n$ is finite and the quotient transitions are surjective. The DVR expansion writes $\ell=u\varpi^r$ with $r>0$; hence $\ell^n$ kills $A_n$. Multiplication by $\varpi^n$ is injective, and the two-term finite free complex $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$ has only cohomology $A_n$ in degree zero. Thus $A_n$ is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. These are precisely the ring assumptions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] for $I=(\varpi)$: finite perfect quotients and torsion $R/I$. The integral coefficient sheaf is its inverse-limit sheaf $R_T$, not the discrete constant sheaf. The integral input category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] includes derived completeness, the uniform interval and compatible etale-origin reductions. Replacing the positive index $n$ by $n+1$ gives exactly the indexing used by the smooth coefficient theorems.

source.place: Clause (4): finite, completed and transported coefficient domains.

proof.text: At finite etale level, apply [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] when $f$ is proper to the underlying abelian complex. Its input is bounded below with torsion cohomology. The final equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] transfers invertibility to the specified constant-module mate, retaining the source and target comparisons of that lemma. When $g$ is smooth, apply [sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change]. To match its diagram (the square of the smooth base change theorem it refers to, with $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$), its smooth map $f:X\to S$ is our $g:Y'\to Y$, its quasi-compact quasi-separated map $g:T\to S$ is our $f:X\to Y$, its $h$ is our $f':X'\to Y'$, and its $e$ is our $g':X'\to X$; Steps 5, 7, 8 and 9 use this matching of roles, whatever the position of the arrows in the cited squares. Our $f$ is qcqs by Step 1. Every $A_n$-cohomology sheaf is killed by $\ell^n$, an invertible integer on $Y$, so it lies in the allowable-torsion category of that theorem. Its exchange is therefore invertible; the same forget-coefficients equivalence identifies this with the module exchange. This proves the finite etale ordinary assertion for the actual map, without requiring that $K$ be bounded above.

source.place: Clause (4): bounded-below proper and smooth base change; Stacks 0DDE (lemma-proper-base-change).

proof.text:
For a finite pro-etale input with witness $\alpha:
u_X^*L\simeq K$, use [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange]. Its hypothesis on $f,f'$ is qcqs, verified in Step 1. In its notation the equality is $T_L
u_{Y'}^*(E_L)=\operatorname{Ex}^R_{
u_X^*L}S_L$, with $S_L,T_L$ isomorphisms. Thus an invertible etale $E_L$ gives an invertible actual pro-etale mate, and naturality in the isomorphism $\alpha$ gives the same conclusion at $K$. In the proper case this is also the precise domain of [thm-weil-pbc-finite-level-proetale], allowing bounded-below witnessed inputs. In the smooth case retain the bounded constructible witness: [sbc-thm-finite-proetale-smooth-base-change], with the diagram labels of Step 4, identifies the same ambient mate with the conjugate etale exchange. It explicitly asserts an isomorphism in the ambient derived category and does not assert bounded constructible endpoints. A finite-Tor input is a restriction of this bounded constructible input domain.

source.place: Clause (4): etale-origin finite pro-etale transport, including named-map identification.

proof.text: For proper $f$ at $R$, apply [thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale] to the specified compatible reduction witnesses of $K$. Step 3 supplies its adic datum, and $f$ is proper by hypothesis. This yields invertibility of its completed exchange, the ordered Rlim composite built from the transported finite-level exchanges, using completed pullback. The item's integral map is the completed adjunction mate; [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] states that, under the canonical finite-reduction and direct-image/derived-limit comparisons, this mate is the completed exchange obtained from the finite-level exchanges, and by Step 5 those are the actual finite pro-etale mates. So the mate is invertible, and its raw rationalization is the map used at $E$ in Step 8. For the constructible domain apply [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete]: every corner is Noetherian and finite-dimensional by Step 1, both $f$ and $f'$ are proper, $\ell$ annihilates $R/I$ and is invertible on all corners, and the geometric fibres have the nonnegative bound $e$ of Step 2. Its component is explicitly the same completed exchange, now with both endpoints in the uniform completed constructible categories. No assertion about discrete integral etale coefficients is used.

source.place: Clause (4): completed proper exchange and its constructible restriction; Stacks 09C9 (theorem-proper-base-change).

proof.text:
For smooth $g$ at $R$, apply [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change], with the diagram relabeling of Step 4 and the index shift of Step 3. Its input corner $T$ is our $X$ and its output corner $X$ is our $Y'$, so both finite-dimension assumptions hold. The input reductions are bounded constructible etale-origin complexes as required in the item; Step 3 gives the finite perfect quotients of invertible torsion order. The theorem yields invertibility of the canonical completed adjunction-mate exchange in the ambient complete category. For its stronger conclusion require a single interval $[a,b]$, independent of $n$, for all four finite-level objects, in our labels
$$Rf_{n,*}K_n,\quad Lg_n^*Rf_{n,*}K_n,\quad Lg_n'^*K_n,\quad Rf'_{n,*}Lg_n'^*K_n,$$
with constructible cohomology. Exactly the final paragraph of the theorem then places both exchange endpoints in $D^b_c(Y',R)$. The first, ambient conclusion uses no such landing claim. The item retains these additional hypotheses wherever it asserts the constructible conclusion.

source.place: Clause (4): integral smooth exchange, with separate uniform constructible landing.

proof.text: For proper ordinary exchange at $E$, use [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension]. Its geometric hypotheses were verified in Steps 1--2, and it defines the rational exchange to be the extension of the completed integral one, so it applies to the specified lattice presentation. For smooth ordinary exchange, the chosen lattice is finite-level etale admissible in the sense of [sbc-def-admissible-lattices]. Apply [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] with the labels of Step 4. Its functors and exchange are raw scalar localizations of the completed integral ones. The theorem yields the ambient exchange at $K_E$, independent of the chosen lattice isomorphism. Its $D^b_c$ conclusion requires square-constructible admissibility, namely the very four families and common interval of Step 7 applied to the lattice. Hence the item makes exactly that distinction between the ambient isomorphism and its constructible restriction, with no finite reduction of a rational object being taken.

source.place: Clause (4): rational ordinary exchange on specified admissible lattice domains.

proof.text: For proper ordinary exchange at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, apply [thm-weil-pbc-qbar]: its component is the finite-stage exchange after passage to a common finite overfield and is independent of the representative. For smooth ordinary exchange use [sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch], with the labels of Step 4. The item assumes its finite-stage $E$ hypotheses for the representatives and their stability under common finite overfields, not just the existence of an arbitrary lattice. That theorem identifies the ambient component with the canonical raw $E$ exchange through the identity-idempotent inclusion and identifies its further-stage components with scalar extensions. It asserts no constructible landing. Restrict only when the additional landing hypotheses retained in the item put the relevant finite-stage values in $D^b_c$; Step 8 then supplies their isomorphism there. These finite-stage values and maps represent the common-stage constructible operations by [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category].

source.place: Clause (4): ordinary common-stage exchange, with the ambient/constructible distinction retained.

proof.text: For finite compact-support exchange choose $c=(j,p)$ from Step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], $j_!K$ is still bounded below for bounded finite torsion etale $K$: its cohomology is $j_!\mathcal H^i(K)$, so it is still annihilated by the same finite coefficient ring. Step 4 applies proper base change to $p$. Follow that invertible proper exchange by $Rp'_*$ of the natural invertible open comparison of [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. This is exactly the compactification formula, and [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] identifies it with its compactification-independent map, with the stated refinement comparisons. Neither factor requires smoothness of $g$. On a finite pro-etale input with a witness, [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] identifies the transported compactification composite with the etale one conjugated by the witness, and asserts its invertibility and independence of the witness. Thus the compact-support claim holds on both finite domains in the item.

source.place: Clause (4): finite compact-support exchange from proper exchange followed by open base change.

proof.text: At $R$, apply [thm-cbc-complete-proetale] to the compactification of Step 2 and the complete input with its compatible etale-origin reductions. Its specified ordered composite is completed proper exchange on $j_!K$, followed by the completed open comparison, and its statement proves invertibility and compactification independence for precisely that composite. Use [thm-cbc-finite-extension] at $E$ on the raw rationalization of the integral category: Step 1 verifies all four Noetherian finite-dimensional schemes and the invertible prime. Its specified exchange is the extension of the completed one, and its statement gives landing in $D^b_c$, naturality for rational morphisms, and independence of the lattice. Finally [thm-cbc-qbar] applies at every admissible common coefficient stage and identifies its component with the finite-stage exchange after a common overfield; its stated independence of field and representative gives the required common-stage map. For these applications the complete integral inputs have compatible etale-origin reductions in a uniform interval; the rational inputs have their specified integral lattice presentations, and the algebraically closed inputs have admissible common-stage presentations with the finite-stage uniform landing bounds. None imposes smoothness on $g$.

source.place: Clause (4): completed, rational and common-stage compact-support exchanges.

proof.text: It remains to identify the package maps and their equations, rather than just prove existence of unrelated endpoint isomorphisms. Apply [fix-lem-exchanges] on the domains just verified. Its finite ordinary map is the constant-module mate, its witnessed pro-etale ordinary map is the ambient ringed mate, its finite compact-support map is the compactification composite, its integral maps are the completed mate and completed compactification composite, and its field maps are their rational and common-stage transports. Clause (1) identifies the compact-support maps with the cited base-change theorem maps; clause (3) identifies smooth ordinary exchange with smooth base change in the exchanged diagram labels. The proper identifications were supplied in Steps 4--6 and 8--9. Clauses (2) and (4) give identity, horizontal and vertical pasting, refinement independence, and compatibility with composition, with the canonical composition maps inserted. Apply these equations only where the intermediate inputs and composite functors satisfy the indicated domains. This proves exactly the coherence asserted in the item; invertibility does not silently enlarge any of those domains.
